re: counter vs consensus, this article on retail shitcos is the one I mentioned:

https://t.co/SoTAdaYKmq

but u can even apply this same principle to SALP, where the “counter” ideas in TMT/shitcos = the ADBE’s or whatever else he was short

obviously adbe isn’t a shitco like abercrombie but there’s clearly defined “AI winners vs AI losers”, he was long too many of the former (consensus), short too many of the latter (counter), and even without leverage, in a multi-mgr L/S model the negative “spread” generated on these pairs will kill u

if ur “secular AI winner” longs are all down 30-50%, and ur SaaS shorts are up 10-20% - which to my untrained eye looks like how July went - u are smoked…even if u don’t blow up u are in such a nasty draw that ur mental capital gets toasted 

so this is why an experienced PM would’ve layered in some long doodoo and short “winners”

it’s part of a morning premkt routine, u just run thru the book “counter, counter, consensus, counter, consensus” and make sure you aren’t too skewed one way or the other

and to go back to the QT point, as an analyst, this is why an ability to consistently generate “counter” ideas is highly valued.

quotedTweet.text:
on idea gen / versatility / “counter” vs “consensus”

1/3

most ideas fit into one of two buckets, consensus, or counter-consensus

multi-mgr L/S has drastically changed this dynamic relative to 10-15 years ago

old: example Tiger cub portfolio of “long tech disruptors vs short the disrupted”

nflx vs cable, amzn vs brick & mortar, etc

but u can’t do that now in multi mgr, the mandate and portfolio constraints are too rigid

2/3

if ur longs are all nflx amzn ("quality," "compounders" etc) and ur shorts are all shitco junk, theres problems from all angles

>blowing up in an unwind
>"you're just making factor bets"
>too rigid / no versatility in idea gen
>if ur an emerging mgr, LPs have become less willing to pay L/S fees for what is mostly long beta/quality/owning 5 of the top 10 S&P components

most of this is understood or above my pay grade or sort of tangential to the main point, which is idea gen

3/3

for a young analyst re: idea generation, vs 10-15 years ago, the biggest difference is that in a coverage model of say 50 names, ur ideas have to cover the whole spectrum

there is a natural inclination to buy good co's and sell bad co's, which is why I'm RTing that mauboussin quote:  “Perhaps the single greatest error in the investment business is a failure to distinguish between the knowledge of a company’s fundamentals and the expectations implied by the market price.”

you have to also develop the "long counter-consensus shitco" skillset, and "short quality compounder" skillset, or identifying great-to-good situations

like, read that retail article I wrote last week on buying shitcos, theres some good stuff in there on how to think abt it

this skillset is one u will have to master regardless if ur goal is to make it "all the way" and run $10B in GMV, the notion of having quality ideas and shitco ideas both ways

if there's 50 names, u want 25 consensus and 25 counter.

versatility is the operative word, and I think the one which has become more highly valued as a trait relative to 10 years ago...
